question.text: Under Regulation 91(C)(ii) of the SEBI LODR Regulations, the annual non-financial disclosures by a Not-for-Profit Organization registered on SSE must be made within what period?

answer.text: 30 days from the end of the financial year.
60 days from the end of the financial year.
90 days from the end of the financial year.
By October 31st of each year along with the financial disclosures.

explanation.text: The Logic: Regulation 91(C)(ii) specifies that non-financial disclosures shall be made within 60 days from the end of the financial year (or such period as SEBI may specify). Financial-aspect disclosures follow a separate, later window tied to the income-tax return date. The Trap: 30 days / 90 days are not 91(C) timelines. October 31st is the financial-aspect date under 91(C)(i), not the non-financial date. Students often collapse both into one deadline - regulators treat them separately. Cross-Exam Context: III-A/III-C tests main-board annual-report timelines (120 days / 60 days for financial results). XXIII tests the SSE NPO split: 60-day non-financial vs Oct-31/ITR financial. Assessor's Pro-Tip: Create two separate engagement letters (or two scope paragraphs) for the 60-day non-financial pack and the Oct-31 financial pack. Different management personnel typically sign the non-financial pack (Program Head) vs the financial pack (CFO), and a single combined scope invites sign-off delays.
